items.q: How does Candow explain creatine's energy role?
items.a: If **Batman is ATP**, creatine is **Robin** — it replenishes energy currency during high-intensity work. The body synthesizes only **1–3 g/day**; ~**95%** is stored in muscle.

items.q: Where does creatine sit in the health toolbox?
items.a: **Weight training is the hammer**; creatine is the multi-purpose wrench. Fat loss from creatine is **indirect** via lean mass and metabolic health — not a fat burner like caffeine.

items.q: Who tends to respond most dramatically?
items.a: **Vegans** — no dietary creatine from animal flesh — fill the largest gap. Postmenopausal women are also strong responders for bone/muscle/brain (estrogen linked to synthesis enzymes).

items.q: What dose tiers does Candow recommend?
items.a: ~**5 g/day** for muscle; **8–12 g** for bone (with resistance training); brain often ~**10 g** safety net; **stressed brains** (sleep deprivation, jet lag, exams) may need **20–30 g acutely** because creatine struggles through the blood-brain barrier.

items.q: Do you need to load, and which form works?
items.a: Loading (**4×5 g/day**) saturates fast but causes GI issues + transient water; **3–5 g/day for ~30 days** reaches the same saturation. Only **creatine monohydrate**, third-party tested (CreaPure, NSF) — James Smith found ~**90%** of shelf gummies had no creatine.
**Timing is irrelevant** (paper accepted around the recording). Candow takes ~**10 g/day** baseline, **20–25 g** after jet lag; consistency beats dose perfection.

items.q: Which creatine myths does the interview debunk?
items.a: Kidney "damage" is often a **creatinine false positive**; water retention from loading is **transient**; not men-only; **no hair-loss evidence**; cramps may fall via super-hydration. A **25,000+** case review supports safety even at **>10 g/day** for years.

items.q: How fast does sedentary muscle loss accelerate after 40?
items.a: About **1% muscle/year** and **1–3% strength/year** after 40 if sedentary. Resistance training plateaus the decline — never too late (even **80–100** still benefit).

Alzheimer's protocol (**20 g × 8 weeks** → **+11%** brain creatine); depression adjunct (**5 g + SSRI** doubled remission in one trial); sleep-deprived (**21 hr**) study used a **30 g** bolus; Stroop test improved with **20 g** over ~90 min.

items.q: Can creatine help bone without lifting?
items.a: No — **8–12 g with weight training** slowed hip BMD loss in postmenopausal women (2-year trial); **never shown without exercise**.
